title: The Airport
dek: A terminal cut open: check-in, security and the gate upstairs, baggage reclaim and arrivals below, and a plane at the jet bridge.

truefalse.s: The plane is outside the airport.
There is a clock on the wall.
The suitcase at check-in is red.
There are four seats at the gate.
The departures board is above the check-in desk.
The passenger at check-in is holding a passport.
The escalator goes from arrivals up to departures.
The backpack is on the floor.
There are four bags on the carousel.
The security officer is standing next to the metal detector.
The jet bridge goes from the gate to the plane door.
The engine is under the wing.
The information desk is in departures.
You can see a pilot through the cockpit window.

A1: Where do you want to fly? Why?
What is in your suitcase when you go on holiday?
Look at the gate. Write five sentences about it.
A2: Describe your journey through the airport, from check-in to the plane. Use first, then, after that.
You are at the check-in desk. Write the dialogue with the agent.
Tell a story about a trip that went wrong. Use the past simple.
B1: Your bag didn't arrive. Write an email to the airline.
Is flying the best way to travel? Think about time, price and the planet.
Give advice to someone flying for the first time. Use should, must and don't forget to.

rooms.ex: We need to be at the airport two hours before the flight.
rooms.def: A place where planes land and take off, with buildings for passengers.

rooms.ex: Check-in closes 45 minutes before the flight.
rooms.def: The desk where you show your ticket and leave your big bags.

rooms.ex: It took twenty minutes to get through security.
rooms.def: The place where they check your bags and you walk through a scanner.

rooms.ex: Flight BA216 is now boarding at gate 12.
rooms.def: The door where you get on the plane.

rooms.ex: Our suitcases were the last ones in baggage reclaim.
rooms.def: The place where you collect your bags after a flight.
The part of the airport where people come out after they land.

parts.ex: Check the departures board for your gate.
parts.def: A big screen that shows the flights, the times and the gates.

parts.ex: Take your bags to the check-in desk.
parts.def: The desk where you check in for your flight.

parts.ex: My suitcase is too heavy - 25 kilos!
parts.def: A case with a handle for carrying clothes when you travel.

parts.ex: All passengers must show their passports.
parts.def: A person who travels on a plane, a train or a bus.

parts.ex: Don't forget your passport!
parts.def: A small book that shows who you are, for travelling to other countries.

parts.ex: The security officer asked me to take off my belt.
parts.def: A person whose job is to check people and bags at the airport.

parts.ex: The metal detector beeped because of my keys.
parts.def: A frame you walk through that beeps if you have metal on you.

parts.ex: Put your bag and your laptop through the scanner.
parts.def: A machine that looks inside your bags.

parts.ex: Put your phone and keys in the tray.
parts.def: A flat plastic box for your things at security.

parts.ex: Look at the clock - our flight leaves in an hour!
parts.def: A thing on the wall that shows the time.

parts.ex: Take the escalator down to arrivals.
parts.def: Moving stairs that carry people up or down.

parts.ex: Our gate number is 12.
parts.def: The number of the gate where your plane is waiting.

parts.ex: Please have your boarding pass ready.
parts.def: A card that lets you get on the plane. It shows your seat number.

parts.ex: There are no free seats at the gate.
parts.def: Places to sit.

parts.ex: I only take a backpack when I fly.
parts.def: A bag you carry on your back.

parts.ex: You can see the planes from the window.
parts.def: An opening in a wall with glass, to let in light.

parts.ex: Our bags are on carousel number 3.
parts.def: The moving belt where your bags come out after the flight.

parts.ex: How much luggage have you got?
parts.def: All the bags and suitcases you take on a journey.

parts.ex: Put the suitcases on a trolley.
parts.def: A metal basket on wheels for carrying bags.

parts.ex: Ask at the information desk where the buses go from.
parts.def: A desk where you can ask questions.

parts.ex: The exit is on the right, after the café.
parts.def: The way out of a building.

parts.ex: I held up a sign with her name on it.
parts.def: A board with words on it. People hold them up to find someone.

parts.ex: The plane lands at six o'clock.
parts.def: A vehicle with wings that flies.

parts.ex: Children can sometimes visit the cockpit after the flight.
parts.def: The front part of a plane where the pilots sit.

parts.ex: The pilot says we'll land in twenty minutes.
parts.def: The person who flies a plane.

parts.ex: I had a window seat over the wing.
parts.def: One of the two long flat parts of a plane that help it fly.

parts.ex: A plane like this has two engines.
parts.def: The machine that makes a plane move.

parts.ex: We walked along the jet bridge onto the plane.
parts.def: A covered bridge from the gate to the plane door.

parts.ex: The flight attendant showed me to my seat.
parts.def: A person who looks after passengers on a plane.

parts.ex: The bags go to the plane on a baggage cart.
parts.def: A small trailer that carries bags to and from the plane.

parts.ex: Baggage handlers work outside in all weather.
parts.def: A person who loads bags onto planes.

parts.ex: The control tower gave the plane permission to land.
parts.def: A tall building where people tell the pilots when to land and take off.
